faq.question: What is the best quality setting for JPEG compression?
faq.answer: For most use cases, quality 85-90 provides the best balance between file size and visual quality. Use 95+ for archival purposes and 70-85 for web optimization.

faq.question: Should I enable progressive JPEG?
faq.answer: Yes, progressive JPEG is recommended for web use as it allows images to load gradually, improving perceived loading speed and user experience.

faq.question: Can I compress JPEG images multiple times?
faq.answer: While possible, re-compressing JPEG images will cause additional quality loss. It's best to always work with original uncompressed images when possible.

faq.question: What's the difference between lossy and lossless compression?
faq.answer: JPEG uses lossy compression, permanently removing some data to reduce file size. For lossless compression, consider PNG format instead.

faq.question: How much can I reduce JPEG file sizes?
faq.answer: JPEG compression can typically reduce file sizes by 60-90% depending on the original image and quality settings, while maintaining excellent visual quality.

faq.question: What color space should I use?
faq.answer: sRGB is recommended for web use as it's the standard color space for most displays. Use Adobe RGB only for professional printing workflows.

notes.title: Compression Level
notes.content: Higher compression levels (6-9) provide better compression but slower processing. Level 6 is usually optimal.

faq.question: What is the best compression level for PNG?
faq.answer: Compression level 6 provides the best balance between file size reduction and processing speed. Levels 8-9 offer maximum compression but take longer to process.

faq.question: Should I enable color optimization?
faq.answer: Yes, color optimization can significantly reduce PNG file sizes by optimizing color palettes without affecting visual quality, especially for images with limited colors.

faq.question: Can PNG compression be lossy?
faq.answer: Standard PNG is always lossless, but some advanced tools offer lossy PNG compression. For lossy compression, consider WebP or JPEG formats.

faq.question: How do I preserve transparency in PNG?
faq.answer: Ensure 'Preserve Transparency' is enabled. This maintains the alpha channel, essential for logos, icons, and graphics with transparent backgrounds.

faq.question: When should I use PNG vs JPEG?
faq.answer: Use PNG for graphics, logos, screenshots, and images with transparency. Use JPEG for photographs and complex images without transparency needs.

faq.question: Can PNG files be compressed multiple times?
faq.answer: Yes, PNG compression is lossless, so you can compress PNG files multiple times without quality loss, unlike JPEG.

faq.answer: WebP is a modern image format developed by Google that provides 25-35% better compression than JPEG while maintaining superior quality and supporting transparency.

faq.question: Should I use lossy or lossless WebP?
faq.answer: Use lossy WebP for photographs and complex images (quality 70-90). Use lossless WebP for graphics and images requiring exact reproduction.

faq.question: How much smaller are WebP files?
faq.answer: WebP files are typically 25-35% smaller than JPEG files with similar quality, and 25-50% smaller than PNG files while supporting transparency.

faq.question: Do all browsers support WebP?
faq.answer: Modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) support WebP. For older browsers, consider providing JPEG/PNG fallbacks.

faq.question: Can WebP replace both JPEG and PNG?
faq.answer: Yes, WebP can replace both formats. Use lossy WebP for photos and lossless WebP for graphics with transparency.

faq.question: What's the best quality setting for WebP?
faq.answer: For web use, quality 75-85 provides excellent compression with minimal quality loss. For archival purposes, use lossless mode.

faq.question: How many colors should I use for GIF compression?
faq.answer: Use 128-256 colors for good quality, 64-128 for smaller files, and 32-64 for maximum compression. Quality decreases with fewer colors.

faq.question: Should I enable dithering?
faq.answer: Enable dithering to maintain visual quality when reducing colors. It helps create smoother gradients and better color transitions.

faq.question: Can I compress animated GIFs?
faq.answer: Yes, our compressor supports both static and animated GIFs. Animation will be preserved during compression.

faq.question: What's the difference between GIF and other formats?
faq.answer: GIF supports animation and transparency but is limited to 256 colors. For photos, use JPEG or WebP. For graphics with many colors, consider PNG.

faq.question: How much can I reduce GIF file sizes?
faq.answer: GIF compression can typically reduce file sizes by 30-70% depending on the original image and color settings used.

faq.question: Should I use interlaced GIFs?
faq.answer: Interlaced GIFs load progressively but are larger. Use for large images where progressive loading improves user experience.
